summary: Processing HTML form data with one-dimensional arrays and loops, and writing program code in a good programming style.

blocks.content: A **data structure** that stores **many values of the same type** under **one identifier**; each element is accessed by its **index**.

<?php
$marks = [7, 9, 4, 10];
$marks[] = 8;                       // add an element at the end
echo count($marks);                 // 5
echo $marks[0];                     // 7
$marks[2] = 6;                      // change the third element
sort($marks);                       // 6 7 8 9 10
?>

blocks.title: Pseudocode arrays
blocks.content:
In Cambridge-style pseudocode arrays are usually declared with bounds and often start at 1:
`DECLARE Marks : ARRAY[1:30] OF INTEGER`
Several form fields with the same name followed by `[]` arrive in PHP as an **array**.

<form action="marks.php" method="post">

  <input type="number" name="mark[]"> <input type="number" name="mark[]">

</form>

blocks.title: Standard algorithms on an array
items: **Total / average:** start `total ← 0`, add every element, divide by the length.
**Maximum / minimum:** start with the first element, compare each element, keep the larger/smaller.
**Counting:** start `count ← 0`, add 1 when the condition is true.
**Linear search:** compare each element with the target until it is found or the array ends.

items.title: Meaningful identifiers
items.content: `$averageMark`, not `$x`. Use a consistent style (camelCase or snake_case).

items.title: Comments
items.content: Explain **why** the code does something, and describe each function.

items.title: Indentation and spacing
items.content: Indent the body of every IF, loop and function so the structure is visible.

items.title: Constants
items.content: `define("MAX_STUDENTS", 30);` instead of "magic numbers" in the code.

items.title: Functions / procedures
items.content: Split the program into small, reusable subroutines with one task each.

items.title: Validation and error handling
items.content: Check input data and handle errors (e.g. a failed database connection).

// Poor
$a=$_POST["p"];if($a<1000){$b=$a*1.3;}else{$b=$a*1.15;}echo $b;

// Good
const MARKUP_CHEAP     = 1.30;   // +30% for goods under 1000 tenge
const MARKUP_EXPENSIVE = 1.15;   // +15% otherwise

function sellingPrice(float $price): float {
    return $price < 1000 ? $price * MARKUP_CHEAP : $price * MARKUP_EXPENSIVE;
}

$price = (float)$_POST["price"];
echo "Selling price: " . sellingPrice($price);
?>
blocks.caption: Poor style vs good style

blocks.content: Good style makes code easier to **read, debug and maintain**, especially when someone else has to change it later — that is the reason to give in "explain why" questions.
